cards.title: open() and modes
cards.body_tr: Dosya işleri `open('ad', mod)` ile başlar. Modlar: `r` oku (varsayılan, dosya yoksa hata), `w` yaz (var olanı siler, yoksa oluşturur), `a` sonuna ekle, `x` yeni oluştur (varsa hata). `t` metin, `b` ikili (resim vb.). Tarayıcıda gerçek diskin yerine sanal bir dosya sistemi var; güvenle dene.
cards.body: File work starts with `open('name', mode)`. Modes: `r` read (default, error if missing), `w` write (erases existing, creates if missing), `a` append, `x` create new (error if exists). `t` text, `b` binary (images etc.). The browser has a virtual file system instead of your disk; safe to try.

cards.statement_tr: `'w'` modu dosyanın eski içeriğini silip üzerine yazar.
cards.statement: Mode `'w'` erases the old content and writes anew.

cards.section: Opening Files for Writing and Updating
cards.title: First, write a file
cards.body_tr: `with open(...) as f:` bloğu dosyayı iş bitince kendisi kapatır; `close()` unutma derdi yoktur. `f.write()` yazıyı dosyaya koyar.
cards.body: A `with open(...) as f:` block closes the file itself when done, so you cannot forget `close()`. `f.write()` puts text in the file.
cards.code:
with open('example.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('This is the first line.\nThis is the second line.')
print(open('example.txt').read())
cards.expected_output:
This is the first line.
This is the second line.

cards.title: read(): everything
cards.body_tr: `read()` tüm metni tek yazı olarak verir. `read(10)` yalnız ilk 10 karakteri okur.
cards.body: `read()` returns all text as one string. `read(10)` reads only the first 10 characters.
cards.code:
with open('example.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('This is the first line.\nThis is the second line.')
f = open('example.txt')
print(type(f.read(10)))
f.seek(0)
print(f.read(10))
f.close()

with open('example.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('This is the first line.\nThis is the second line.')
with open('example.txt') as f:
    print(repr(f.readline()))
cards.why_tr: `readline()` ilk satırı sonundaki `\n` ile birlikte okur; `repr` bunu görünür yapar.
cards.why: `readline()` reads the first line including its trailing `\n`; `repr` makes it visible.

cards.title: readline, readlines, splitlines
cards.body_tr: `readline()` tek satır, `readlines()` satırlar listesi (sonlarda `\n` ile), `read().splitlines()` ise `\n` olmadan satırlar listesi verir.
cards.body: `readline()` gives one line, `readlines()` a list of lines (with `\n`), and `read().splitlines()` a list without `\n`.
cards.code:
with open('example.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('This is the first line.\nThis is the second line.')
with open('example.txt') as f:
    print(f.readlines())
with open('example.txt') as f:
    print(f.read().splitlines())
cards.expected_output:
['This is the first line.\n', 'This is the second line.']
['This is the first line.', 'This is the second line.']

cards.code:
with open('example.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('This is the first line.\nThis is the second line.')
with open('example.txt') as f:
    lines = f.read().___()
print(len(lines))

cards.section: Opening Files for Writing and Updating
cards.title: Append with 'a', overwrite with 'w'
cards.body_tr: `'a'` mevcut içeriğin sonuna ekler. `'w'` her şeyi silip baştan yazar. Farkı gör.
cards.body: `'a'` adds to the end of existing content. `'w'` wipes everything and writes anew. See the difference.
cards.code:
with open('example.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('This is the first line.\nThis is the second line.')
with open('example.txt', 'a') as f:
    f.write('\nAppended!')
print(open('example.txt').read().splitlines())
with open('example.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('Only me')
print(open('example.txt').read())
cards.expected_output:
['This is the first line.', 'This is the second line.', 'Appended!']
Only me

cards.section: Opening Files for Writing and Updating
cards.code:
with open('t.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('A')
with open('t.txt', 'a') as f:
    f.write('B')
with open('t.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('C')
print(open('t.txt').read())

cards.title: Deleting files
cards.body_tr: `os.remove(yol)` dosyayı siler; yoksa hata verir. Önce `os.path.exists` ile kontrol etmek iyi alışkanlıktır.
cards.body: `os.remove(path)` deletes a file and errors if missing. Checking `os.path.exists` first is a good habit.
cards.expected_output:
deleted
The file does not exist

cards.title: What is JSON?
cards.body_tr: JSON, bir sözlüğün **yazı** halidir ve dosyalarda/ağda veri taşımak için çok kullanılır. JSON'da tür yoktur, her şey yazıdır. Dikkat: JSON çift tırnak ister, Python sözlüğü tek de olabilir.
cards.body: JSON is the **text** form of a dictionary, widely used to move data in files and over networks. JSON has no types; it is all text. Note: JSON requires double quotes, Python dicts may use single.

cards.statement: JSON is really plain text (a str).
cards.why_tr: Ağda ve dosyada yazı olarak taşınır; `loads` ile sözlüğe dönüşür.
cards.why: It travels as text in files and networks; `loads` turns it into a dict.

cards.title: json.loads: text to dict
cards.body_tr: `json.loads(yazı)` JSON yazısını Python sözlüğüne çevirir. (loads = load string)
cards.body: `json.loads(text)` converts a JSON string into a Python dict. (loads = load string)
cards.code:
import json

person_json = '{"name": "Asabeneh", "country": "Finland", "skills": ["React", "Python"]}'
person_dct = json.loads(person_json)
print(type(person_dct).__name__)
print(person_dct['name'])
print(person_dct['skills'])

cards.title: json.dumps: dict to text
cards.body_tr: `json.dumps(sözlük, indent=4)` sözlüğü okunur biçimli JSON yazısına çevirir. Çıktının türü `str`'dir.
cards.body: `json.dumps(dict, indent=4)` turns a dict into nicely formatted JSON text. The result is a `str`.
cards.code:
import json

person = {'name': 'Asabeneh', 'skills': ['Python', 'React']}
person_json = json.dumps(person, indent=4)
print(type(person_json).__name__)
print(person_json)

cards.why_tr: JSON `true` küçük harfle yazar ve çift tırnak kullanır.
cards.why: JSON writes `true` in lowercase and uses double quotes.

cards.title: json.dump: save to a file
cards.body_tr: `json.dump(veri, dosya, indent=4)` sözlüğü doğrudan dosyaya yazar (`dumps` yazı döndürür, `dump` dosyaya yazar). Sonra `json.load` ile geri okuyabilirsin.
cards.body: `json.dump(data, file, indent=4)` writes a dict straight into a file (`dumps` returns text, `dump` writes to a file). Read it back with `json.load`.
cards.code:
import json

person = {'name': 'Asabeneh', 'city': 'Helsinki'}
with open('json_example.json', 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    json.dump(person, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=4)
with open('json_example.json') as f:
    print(json.load(f))

cards.title: CSV: comma separated values
cards.body_tr: CSV, tablo verisini düz metin olarak saklar; satır = kayıt, virgül = sütun ayırıcı. `csv.reader` satırları liste olarak verir. İlk satır genelde sütun adlarıdır.
cards.body: CSV stores tables as plain text; row = record, comma = column separator. `csv.reader` gives each row as a list. The first row is usually the column names.
cards.expected_output:
Column names are: name, country, city
Asabeneh lives in Finland, Helsinki.

cards.why: The second row is `['c', 'd']`; item 0 is 'c'.

cards.title: Excel files
cards.body_tr: Excel dosyalarını okumak için `xlrd` gibi ek bir **paket** gerekir; bunu bir sonraki gün `pip` ile kurmayı öğreneceksin. Bu yüzden burada çalıştırmıyoruz.
cards.body: Reading Excel files needs an extra **package** such as `xlrd`; you will learn to install one with `pip` next day. So we do not run it here.

cards.title: XML: tagged data
cards.body_tr: XML, HTML'e benzer ama etiketleri serbesttir. En üstteki etiket `root`tur; etiketin `attrib`ı özellikleri verir. `xml.etree.ElementTree` ile okunur; burada dosya yerine yazıdan okuyoruz.
cards.body: XML looks like HTML but tags are free-form. The top tag is the `root`; `attrib` gives its attributes. Read it with `xml.etree.ElementTree`; here we parse from text instead of a file.
cards.code:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

xml = '<person gender="female"><name>Asabeneh</name><country>Finland</country></person>'
root = ET.fromstring(xml)
print('Root tag:', root.tag)
print('Attribute:', root.attrib)
for child in root:
    print('field:', child.tag)
cards.expected_output:
Root tag: person
Attribute: {'gender': 'female'}
field: name
field: country

cards.statement_tr: JSON ve XML ikisi de yapılandırılmış veri biçimidir.
cards.statement: JSON and XML are both structured data formats.
cards.why_tr: İkisi de iç içe yapıyı metinle ifade eder.
cards.why: Both express nested structure as text.

cards.title: Summary
points_tr: `open(ad, mod)`: `r` oku, `w` ez, `a` ekle, `x` yeni; `with` dosyayı kendisi kapatır.
CSV ve XML için `csv` ve `xml.etree.ElementTree` kullanılır.
points: `open(name, mode)`: `r` read, `w` overwrite, `a` append, `x` new; `with` closes the file itself.
Use `csv` and `xml.etree.ElementTree` for CSV and XML.
